facts.statement: BlockLibraryDatabaseCache.cachedLibrary (private static Database) — TIER A, SINGLE SLOT. Acquire(path) returns the cached side Database only if path (OrdinalIgnoreCase), LastWriteTimeUtc and Length all match; otherwise it reads a fresh Database, DISPOSES the previously cached one and replaces it. Warm-up effect: a warm-up that acquires a private library copy (different path) EVICTS and disposes the governed library's cached Database and leaves the private copy's Database resident until the next Acquire with a different signature. So a different key does NOT leave the governed key untouched — it removes it (the next governed Acquire re-reads the governed DWG). Not a file-system-only effect: it holds a live in-memory AutoCAD Database.

The public import path cannot target a private library copy by itself: BlockLibraryImporter.EnsureBlocks (and EnsureForPlan/EnsureRequirements through it) always uses LibraryPath => BlockLibraryLocator.ResolvePath(), which is the UserSettings.BlockLibraryPath override or the default <catalogs>/blocks-library.dwg. The availability observer AutoCadExternalLibraryBlockQuery resolves the same path and shares the same single-slot cache. A warm-up using a private copy therefore needs either (a) to write the private path into the user settings file (persistent user-visible side effect, and it changes the governed path for everything that reads settings), or (b) Plugin-internal code calling BlockLibraryDatabaseCache.Acquire(privatePath) directly (the class is internal to RackCad.Plugin), which evicts the governed slot (CORE-02).

facts.statement: The remaining Plugin statics a warm-up could read are tier B: KindHandlerRegistry.Default (get-only, built once, only a readonly _dispatch field), CustomPropertiesExecutor.IsKnownKind (readonly delegate), RackDefinitionCreationResult.NoMissing (readonly empty array) and BlockLibraryImporter.LibraryPath (computed per call).

limitations: The census came from a heuristic scanner (comment-stripping plus regex over `git show 3375aadb:<file>` for every .cs file), not a C# compiler. It was cross-checked against a raw `git grep` of static declarations. For Application, Plugin and Domain the only lines the two disagreed on were operator overloads; for UI they disagreed only on the static constructors and the ShellResources.Dictionary property, which the scanner caught and the raw grep did not.

Tier B ('never written after initialization') rests on pattern searches over src: indexer assignment, Add/TryAdd/GetOrAdd/Remove/Clear/Insert/Sort/Reverse, Array.Sort/Reverse/Clear/Fill, and direct property assignment. Indirect mutation cannot be ruled out by grep: an array passed as IList to a method that writes it, a cast from IReadOnlyList back to an array, or reflection.

The Part 1 facts leave out members whose objects are immutable. These are: 38 DependencyProperty/DependencyPropertyKey registration fields (NumericField 14, RackEditorVisualShell 9, RackBoundedEditorShell 7, EditorActionBar 4, StructuralSectionPicker 2, SelectionMatrix 1, EditorStatusPresenter 1); every static readonly Brush built through UiSupport.FrozenBrush (UiSupport.cs:51-55) or aliasing a frozen brush; static readonly string/double scalars (including the RackFrameConfiguratorLayoutStore paths, RackFrameConfiguratorLayoutStore.cs:25-29, which have a file side effect but no mutable static); and get-only properties holding immutable objects (EditorClosePolicy.cs:16, EditorStatus.cs:36, SelectionMatrixBulkEditor.cs:17,20). Static expression-bodied properties with no backing state are also left out (EditorStatus.cs:56-59, RackSelectiveWindow.xaml.cs:2688,2691, PendingTextField.cs:179, PreviewPalette.cs:54).

For Application, Plugin and Domain the task asked only for tier-A members, so the many tier-B static readonly sentinels (empty arrays, `new List<T>()` exposed as IReadOnlyList, for example src/RackCad.Application/Systems/PushBack/PushBackBootPlan.cs:82) and singletons (SystemRegistry.Default at SystemRegistry.Default.cs:23, FunctionRegistry.Productive, LengthUnits.Authority) are not listed one per member. None showed a run-time write.

Framework behavior is not established from the repository source: System.Text.Json option locking and metadata caching, WPF thread affinity of the unfrozen static SolidColorBrush fields (UI-34..UI-55) and of the shared ResourceDictionary (UI-04), WPF metadata overrides, and AutoCAD Database file handles and locking. Where these matter they are marked UNCERTAIN or described as framework-level.
The tests directory was read only to find callers of the static test seams (Substitute, RedirectForTests). It is not part of the census.

Part 2 was traced by reading the named entry points (LateralHeaderDrawer.CreateSystemBlock, BlockPlacement, BlockLibraryImporter/BlockLibraryDatabaseCache/AutoCadExternalLibraryBlockQuery, RackEmbedStore, SelectivePalletDesignStore, JsonRackCatalogProvider/RackCatalogLoader/CatalogDirectory, RackLog/RackDiagnosticsLog, UserSettingsStore/CorruptFile). Transitive callees that declare no static fields (for example CsvCatalogReader, LayerHelper, BlockNaming) were checked only by the static-member scan, not read line by line.

The warm-up itself does not exist at 3375aadb. Its effects are inferred from the code paths a warm-up would have to call, and whether it would call BlockLibraryDatabaseCache.Acquire directly or go through the settings override is a design choice outside the repository.

verdicts.correction: BlockLibraryDatabaseCache.cachedLibrary (private static Database) is TIER A and a SINGLE SLOT. Acquire(path) returns the cached side Database only if path (OrdinalIgnoreCase on the raw string), LastWriteTimeUtc and Length all match. Otherwise it reads a fresh Database. ONLY IF that read succeeds does it dispose the previously cached Database and replace the slot. If ReadDwgFile throws, the fresh Database is disposed, RackLog.Exception is written (the message includes the path), null is returned, and the previous slot, which may be the governed library, stays intact. So a warm-up that successfully acquires a private copy at a different path evicts and disposes the governed cached Database, and the private copy stays resident until the next Acquire with a different signature. The next governed Acquire then re-reads the governed DWG. The cache is not file-system-only: it holds a live in-memory AutoCAD Database. FileInfo.Length is evaluated outside the try (:21-23), but both callers check File.Exists first.

missed.statement: The UI test host deliberately installs an UNDISPOSED EditorDiscardPrompt substitute (`_ = EditorDiscardPrompt.Substitute(_ => true)`). The 'leaked scope' scenario named in UI-01 is therefore real and intentional in tests/RackCad.UI.Tests, but not in production src. Substitute is PUBLIC, not internal, so any assembly could call it. Nothing in src does.

BlockPlacement.PlaceAndReport and PlaceDefinition are INTERACTIVE: they run an EntityJig through editor.Drag. A non-interactive warm-up cannot exercise them. The only non-interactive placement, AppendReference, locks the given Document and appends to ITS model space, which is the user's drawing rather than a side Database. A 'block reference placement' warm-up on a side Database cannot go through BlockPlacement at all.

missed.statement: CreateSystemBlock appends a piece BlockReference only when the block already exists in the TARGET database's block table. Otherwise it records the piece as missing and skips it, and it never imports from the library itself. On a fresh side Database without a prior BlockLibraryImporter.EnsureBlocks into that same database, the warm-up would therefore draw no piece references and never reach ApplyDynamicParameters. It would create only block definitions, annotations and dimensions.

missed.statement: A second public entry point constructs JsonRackCatalogProvider on an arbitrary directory: CatalogValidator.ValidateDirectory(directory). Any use of it (none in src) adds a permanent cache entry keyed by that raw directory string, alongside the public constructor. Separately, GetOrAdd inserts the entry BEFORE loading, so even a throwing load leaves an empty entry under that key for the process lifetime.

The block-library cache key is the RAW path string, compared OrdinalIgnoreCase with no normalization. A differently spelled path to the governed DWG counts as a different key, which evicts and re-reads, for example a settings override written with other separators or a relative path. A failed read of a warm-up copy writes a RackLog entry containing that path into the shared production log.
